mustKnow.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
mustKnow.snippet: More than 500 passengers were aboard the two trains involved in the crash in Toledo province south of Madrid.
mustKnow.brief: Two trains collided on Wednesday morning about 140km south of Madrid, near the municipalities of Mora and Orgaz, with at least 68 people confirmed dead. A Renfe train reportedly rear-ended a stationary Iryo train after a computer failure had halted several trains and the control centre allowed them to resume without speed limits. Spain's transport minister called the decision inexplicable, and authorities say the death toll could rise further.
mustKnow.why: At least 68 dead; Spain's second high-speed crash in a year

mustKnow.title: The Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged less than a week before the midterms
mustKnow.originalTitle: La Reserva Federal mantiene sin cambios los tipos de interés a menos de una semana de las ‘midterms’
mustKnow.snippet: The Fed kept rates unchanged days before the US midterms, with two dissenting votes for a hike as inflation picks up.
mustKnow.brief: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate steady in the 3.75% to 4% range, a result more than 90% of analysts had expected, less than a week before the U.S. midterm elections. Chair Kevin Warsh said the bank must bring down inflation, which has run above target for nearly six years, and two dissenting governors wanted a quarter-point hike. Analysts put about 85% odds on a rate increase at the December meeting.
mustKnow.why: Two dissents for a hike signal inflation worries before midterms

mustKnow.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Lands in Miami After Fleeing Brazil
mustKnow.snippet: Bolsonaro left Brazil after losing the presidential vote and police cancelled his passport in an investigation, a major Brazilian political development.
mustKnow.brief: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's Brazilian presidential runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, landed in Miami on a private jet with his family after leaving Brazil through Argentina and Ecuador. Brazilian police had canceled his passport as part of an investigation, and he faces several probes at home. He has refused to accept the result and called himself the true president, a claim his own party and international observers do not support.
mustKnow.why: Passport cancelled amid probe; watch for extradition and US response

mustKnow.title: Coalition talks loom in Israel as Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs set to fall short of majority
mustKnow.snippet: Netanyahu has lost his governing majority, and coalition prospects now hinge on whether Jewish opposition parties will work with Palestinian parties.
mustKnow.brief: Netanyahu's governing bloc has lost its majority after Tuesday's election, with both Jewish blocs failing to reach the 61 seats needed. Palestinian-led Arab Israeli parties, heading for a record 16 to 19 seats, now hold the balance, and Eisenkot must decide whether to work with them or let Netanyahu survive through new elections or a unity government. President Isaac Herzog will assign a coalition mandate once all votes, including about 14% of absentee ballots, are counted.
mustKnow.why: Netanyahu loses majority; any government may need Palestinian parties

cleantech.title: DOE announces $10.1B in loans to Constellation, Alliant, for 3.7 GW
cleantech.snippet: The loans could fund uprates at existing plants, a lower-cost route to adding capacity than building new generation.
cleantech.why: Uprates add 3.7 GW cheaply, faster than new builds

cleantech.title: CATL pushes ahead with 20 Ah solid-state EV batteries, with 500 Wh/kg in sight
cleantech.snippet: CATL has advanced its solid-state cells to 20 Ah and targets small-scale production in 2027, aiming for 500 Wh/kg.
cleantech.brief: CATL says its sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries have entered 20 Ah trial production, with a target energy density of 500 Wh/kg. The company expects small-scale production to begin in 2027 and mass production around 2030, with output limited at first. CATL chairman Robin Zeng said the technology has only reached level four on a nine-level scale, and rivals Toyota, Samsung SDI and BYD are targeting similar 2027 timelines.
cleantech.why: Solid-state timeline: small-scale production 2027, 500 Wh/kg target

cleantech.title: Renewables to reach 40% of total generating capacity, beat gas within a year – EIA
cleantech.snippet: EIA data show renewables rising from 37.7% to 40.4% of US capacity within a year, overtaking natural gas and nearly quintupling nuclear.
cleantech.brief: Renewables' share of total US generating capacity is projected to rise from 37.7% to 40.4% over the coming year, passing natural gas and outstripping nuclear about fivefold, according to EIA data reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign. Wind and solar already produced about 21.1% of domestic electricity through August 2026, while coal output fell 8.7%. Battery storage capacity grew 17,586.9 MW over the past year, which the EIA expects to keep expanding.
cleantech.why: Renewables overtake gas in US capacity share within a year

cleantech.title: The cracks in the AI race for onsite gas power
cleantech.snippet: Developers building onsite gas plants for data centres are hitting turbine cracking and fuel price volatility, undermining the quick-power strategy.
cleantech.why: Turbine cracking undercuts the onsite-gas shortcut for data centres

cleantech.title: Kyon Energy puts 282MWh Alfeld battery storage project in Germany into operation
cleantech.snippet: The 137.5MW/282MWh battery plant would be among Germany's largest storage projects to reach operation.
cleantech.brief: Kyon Energy has commissioned and started operating its 137.5MW/282MWh battery energy storage system at Alfeld in Germany. The developer describes it as potentially the largest project of its kind in the country to reach this milestone. The source summary gives no further detail on costs, grid role, or next steps.
cleantech.why: 137.5MW/282MWh, among Germany's largest operating battery plants

cleantech.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
cleantech.snippet: The proposal would rescind a Biden-era rule that cuts methane leaks from oil and gas operations.
cleantech.brief: The Trump administration is seeking to reverse a rule from the Biden era that was meant to cut emissions of methane, a gas that traps far more heat than carbon dioxide. The rule targets leaks and releases from oil and gas operations. If the repeal goes through, those limits on the fossil fuel sector would be lifted, which could raise the climate impact of drilling and production.
cleantech.why: Methane rule rollback shifts oil-and-gas compliance costs

ai.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
ai.snippet: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Carbon as its next frontier model, with details in its official post.
ai.brief: Google DeepMind has announced Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model so far, with strong cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic abilities. It ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59 and posts 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities. Access is limited to a subset of cyber defenders and trusted partners for now, with broader release to developers and consumers planned once guardrails are refined.
ai.why: New DeepMind frontier model, though not yet publicly usable

ai.title: Microsoft posts $92.3bn quarterly revenue after offering buyouts to 60,000 employees
ai.snippet: Azure grew 48% in the September quarter, and Microsoft's results came days after it offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees.
ai.brief: Microsoft beat Wall Street forecasts in its September quarter, reporting total revenue of roughly $92.3bn and profit above $36.6bn, with analysts having expected about $90.6bn and $35.1bn. Its Azure cloud unit was the main driver, expanding 48% and lifting shares that afternoon. The results arrived two days after the company offered voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 staff, about a quarter of its workforce, as it spends heavily on AI.
ai.why: Azure up 48% even as Microsoft offers 60,000 buyouts

ai.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI
ai.snippet: The payments reflect the financial dependence of Microsoft's partnership with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing, in the quarter to September 30.
ai.brief: Microsoft booked roughly $10 billion from its business dealings with OpenAI in the three months ending September 30, according to a regulatory filing made Wednesday. That amount is close to 11% of the company's $92.3 billion total quarterly revenue. The two firms remain financially entangled even as they increasingly chase the same customers, and OpenAI still owes Microsoft $7.2 billion in receivables.
ai.why: $10B quarter shows how tied Microsoft's results are to OpenAI

ai.title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows
ai.snippet: Google's Alphabet revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion in the quarter, while core ad growth slowed as AI Search ads expand worldwide.
ai.why: Core ad growth slowing; AI search ads are Google's hedge

ai.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying
ai.snippet: Anthropic is giving enterprise customers visibility into their model spending, a move ahead of its planned IPO.
ai.brief: Anthropic has launched new reporting tools that let companies' managers see what their teams produced with Claude, how much it cost, and where workflows broke down, using internal analytics and employee surveys. Anthropic says the data won't be used for model training by default, and the reports will suggest ways to improve results. The move addresses a major customer concern about return on investment, as AI token spending grows quickly and many large firms still struggle to see clear gains.
ai.why: Spend-visibility tooling aims at enterprise ROI questions pre-IPO

ai.title: GitHub Octoverse 2026
ai.snippet: GitHub reports merged pull requests tripled to 220 million monthly and commits to 7.38 billion, driven by agentic coding.
ai.brief: GitHub's Octoverse 2026 report, announced at GitHub Universe by EVP Jay Parikh, shows agentic engineering driving sharp growth on the platform. Merged pull requests reached about 220 million a month after roughly tripling in under a year, and commit volume climbed past seven billion monthly, with the bulk of that surge arriving in the latter half of the year. New repository creation also doubled to around 30 million per month, and the report adds breakdowns by industry and by interoperability or reverse engineering projects.
ai.why: Merged PRs tripled to 220M monthly, driven by agentic coding

world.title: Iran war live: Tehran presses 7-day Hormuz plan; Trump denies peace talks
world.snippet: Iran says it is consulting mediators on its seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Trump denies any peace talks are underway.
world.brief: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says Tehran is in close contact with mediators about putting its seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz into practice. The source offers no details on the plan's terms or timeline. It also does not give Donald Trump's response beyond the headline's claim that he denies peace talks are under way, so the wider diplomatic picture remains unclear.
world.why: Hormuz reopening plan matters for oil prices and shipping

world.title: Vicepresidente de EU envía carta a jefe de seguridad de Irán; busca reanudar conversaciones de paz
world.snippet: Trump reportedly directed Vance to contact Iran's Mohsen Rezaei to restart peace talks and head off new US strikes.
world.why: Vance back-channel to Rezaei contradicts Trump's public denials

world.title: Spain’s Transportation Minister Said Incorrect Instructions Led to Train Crash
world.snippet: Spain's transport minister blames traffic control operators for sending a train toward a stopped one, causing the Toledo crash.
world.brief: Spain's transport minister blamed wrong instructions for a rail disaster, saying a faulty choice by control staff pushed one train toward another that was stopped ahead on the line. The crash near Toledo has killed at least 68 people, according to reports, and survivors described carriages packed with badly hurt passengers. Spain's football federation has postponed its matches out of respect for the tragedy.
world.why: Blame falls on traffic control, raising rail safety oversight questions

world.title: Bank of Canada raises interest rates for the first time in three years
world.snippet: The increase, the first in three years, reflects energy-driven inflation pressure, shifting the outlook for borrowing costs.
world.brief: The Bank of Canada raised its key interest rate by a quarter percentage point, its first increase in three years. The central bank acted because soaring energy prices pushed inflation higher. The move makes borrowing costlier across the economy, so households and businesses with loans or mortgages may feel the effect.
world.why: Energy-driven inflation pushes a G7 central bank to hike first

world.title: Venezuela’s Moment of Truth
world.snippet: Opposition leader Machado's return from exile raises questions about Venezuela's political transition and her next steps.
world.brief: Venezuela's most popular opposition politician, María Corina Machado, has returned home after a period in exile, according to a New York Times summary. The feed text does not say how long she was away, what charges or conditions she faced, or what plans she has announced. The piece poses the open question of what happens next, but the available material does not answer it.
world.why: Machado's return tests Venezuela's political transition

world.title: Budget 2026: Healey hikes taxes on banks and landlords to fund £100 handouts to 20m households
world.snippet: Healey's first budget raises bank and landlord taxes to pay for a £100 winter payment, as official forecasts see no end to the cost-of-living squeeze.
world.brief: Chancellor John Healey announced a £100 winter cost-of-living payment for households in council tax bands A-D in England, costing £2.6bn, funded by doubling the bank surcharge on profits to 6% and raising tax on property and savings income by 2p. The Office for Budget Responsibility warned of a grim living standards outlook, with inflation near 4% and the tax rise on rental income risking higher rents. Critics said the handout was badly targeted, and the bank levy lasts only 15 months.
world.why: Bank and landlord taxes fund £100 payments as squeeze persists
